messages:
anya: quick heads-up — the AWQ/GPTQ bakeoff on the CUDA16 nodes just failed for a few models when going through the TRT-LLM path. vLLM fallback works but perf is bad (2-3x latency).

mike: ugh. error logs? stack traces?

anya: pasted the core error from the pod logs:

```
[tensorRT] ERROR: Failed to load plugin 'awq_plugin' : cannot resolve symbol 'cuGetProcAddress'
E tensorflow: TRTPluginLoader: plugin registration failed
```

ravi: that symbol is new in CUDA 16's driver API (cuGetProcAddress). TRT-LLM plugins built against older libcuda/libnvinfer won't find it.

sasha: so probably a libnvinfer/tensorrt mismatch with the distro image. Which TRT version are these nodes using?

anya: nodes are using NV_TENSORRT=8.8.1 and system libs from the nvidia/cuda:16.0 image. CI images for trt-llm we built earlier were linked against 8.6.x.

benchmark-ci: test summary: AWQ-GPTQ mix on mistral-3-small: trt path OOMs or plugin load fails on 3/5 runs. vLLM path (soft-fallback) passes but 95th latency 2.4x higher; p50 about 1.9x higher. Accuracy deltas negligible for AWQ vs GPTQ on eval set.

mike: two options: (1) rebuild TRT-LLM plugins against CUDA16+TRT8.8, or (2) keep using older CUDA images on TRT nodes until we validate. Rebuilding may be quicker if no API break.

ravi: rebuilding is straightforward but beware of symbol versioning: if plugin uses cuGetProcAddress we need driver >= 535.x I think.

sasha: temporary workaround: force the runtime to route these quantized models to vLLM path via model routing policy. Add a per-model flag until trt plugin rebuild is in place.

anya: agreed — I'll flip routing for the affected Mistral3 and Mistral3-mini models to prefer vLLM with a canary rule for 10% traffic to trt when plugin is rebuilt.

mike: note that even when plugin loads, we saw tokenization alignment issues with AWQ in TRT-LLM on longer contexts previously — need a quick eval pass after rebuild.

benchmark-ci: queued a smoke eval run for rebuilt plugin once artifacts available. Patch target: include both TRT8.8 built plugin and a small test that runs 2k tokens to check KV cache correctness.

deploy-bot: deploy request 1981234590 by anya: update model routing for mistral3 -> approved automatically by policy (no infra changes).

ravi: also file an infra ticket to add a node pool label `cuda=16-trt-ready` so we can segregate and roll without touching production default nodes.

anya: creating infra ticket and GH issue on trt-llm repo for rebuild + test matrix (CUDA16, TRT8.8, awq/gptq combos). I'll link stats from benchmark-ci in the issue.

sasha: one more gotcha — if we rebuild with TRT8.8 but the system driver on some hosts is still older, plugin may still fail at load time. We should include a runtime check that verifies driver >= required before scheduling trt jobs.

mike: good call. add a preflight that runs `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` and compare.

anya: action items: (1) router change (done), (2) infra ticket for node pool label (open), (3) GH issue to rebuild trt-llm plugins target TRT8.8+CUDA16 (open), (4) add runtime driver-version preflight (todo). I'll post links when created.

benchmark-ci: posted preliminary numbers to the bakeoff doc: https://internal.redwood/bakeoffs/1981234567 — includes p50/p95, token/sec, eval delta.

mike: thanks. If anyone hits the plugin error and needs a quick local repro, use:

```bash
# repro (on CUDA16 node)
docker run --gpus all -e NV_TENSORRT=8.8.1 -v /opt/trt_plugins:/opt/trt_plugins my/trt-llm:ci ./run_trt_infer.sh --model mistral3-awq
```

ravi: can also validate with `ldd` on the plugin .so to ensure it doesn't reference unknown symbols.

anya: final note — routing to vLLM reduces throughput but buys time. We should prioritize the rebuild + driver compatibility matrix so we can restore trt path for production quant workloads.

mike: tagging infra/eng-ml to keep eyes on the rebuild. :eyes:
